back: Cl₂ pale green gas; Br₂ red-brown liquid (orange-brown vapour); I₂ grey-black solid (purple vapour).
Bromine orange-red; iodine violet. In water: Br₂ orange-yellow, I₂ brown.
Decreases down the group: more electrons, stronger instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces.
Cl–Cl 242 > Br–Br 193 > I–I 151 (larger atoms); F–F only 158 because lone pairs on small F atoms repel.
Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂: smaller atom attracts an incoming electron more strongly (E⦵ more positive).
Cl₂ + 2Br⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + Br₂; Cl₂ + 2I⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + I₂; Br₂ + 2I⁻ → 2Br⁻ + I₂.
F₂ explosive in the dark; Cl₂ explosive in sunlight; Br₂ needs heat + Pt; I₂ slow, reversible.
Decreases HF > HCl > HBr > HI as H–X bond energy falls; HI gives purple iodine with a hot wire.
I₂ + 2S₂O₃²⁻ → 2I⁻ + S₄O₆²⁻; chlorine oxidises thiosulfate to sulfate.
